basis.title: Energy Conservation Program for Certain Industrial Equipment: Energy Conservation Standards and Test Procedures for Commercial Heating, Air-Conditioning, and Water-Heating Equipment (final rule), 77 FR 28928, May 16, 2012
basis.by: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy
basis.label: "DOE used a distribution of lifetimes between 10 and 25 years, with an average of 15 years"; Table V.7 (PDF p.29, printed 28956): "DOE estimated CRAC equipment lifetime ranged between 10 and 25 years, with an average lifespan of 15 years"
basis.note: Printed page 28958. Direct match: all computer room air conditioner classes (the literature did not distinguish classes). The distribution spans 10 to 25 years.

basis.by: U.S. Department of Energy, Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy

open_questions: Every source here is a published planning, design or accounting life. None is observed replacement data.
Some maintenance intervals come from TM 5-692-1, an Army manual for mission-critical (C4ISR) facilities; they may be tighter than typical commercial practice.
